analyst_view.overall: Early view: bottom side Crystal Palace host 18th-placed Manchester United, and both clubs sacked their managers on 12 November. Palace removed Pierre Sage and have not yet named a successor; United dismissed Michael Carrick, and Sky Sports reports they have agreed terms with Mauricio Pochettino, with Al Jazeera also naming him the favourite. Palace play Jagiellonia away in the Europa League on Thursday 10 December, while United host RB Leipzig on the Tuesday; United are also without long-term absentees, with one report saying Benjamin Sesko may be out until early 2027 and Manuel Ugarte and Carlos Baleba facing long spells out.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I lean slightly higher: Palace have the league's worst goal difference (-14) and have conceded more than anyone, and United just drew 4-4 with Villa. New managers often tighten things up, which is why I don't go further.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners. With two new managers and unknown set-ups, nothing points clearly either way yet.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean higher: both sides are in the relegation zone and under heavy pressure, and Palace come in three days after a trip to Poland, which tends to bring late, tired challenges. The referee is not yet known.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots. Both defences have been open, which supports a high number, but United's attack is thinner without Sesko and Palace may be rotated after Thursday, so I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target, which is already high. Weak defending on both sides supports it, but with new managers and unknown line-ups I don't move from it this far out.
